profile.summary: ProGen3 is a family of generative protein language models released by Profluent. Given a direction marker and an optional partial sequence, a model writes amino acids one at a time, in either the N-to-C or the C-to-N direction, and it can also fill in a span in the middle of a given sequence. The same models score an existing sequence by log-likelihood and perplexity, which is how the repository evaluates them on ProteinGym assays. Six checkpoints are published, from 112M to about 3B parameters, under a non-commercial weights licence.

summary_quotes.text: This repository contains code to access the ProGen3 family of models as well as cli interface to run these models for scoring and generation.
The model weights are released under a **non-commercial** usage license.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ProGen3 is a decoder-only transformer whose feed-forward layers are a mixture of 8 experts, 2 of which are used for each token, so a forward pass activates 27% of the parameters. The paper gives a context length of 8192 tokens, SwiGLU feed-forward networks, rotary position embeddings with theta 100000, grouped query attention and pre-layer RMS normalisation, with a load-balancing loss weighted 0.05. The released 3B configuration has 24 layers, hidden size 1280, 16 attention heads, intermediate size 3840 and a vocabulary of 134 tokens, matching the paper's table. It is trained in both reading directions: a prompt starts with 1 for N-to-C or 2 for C-to-N. A separate [GLM] prompt form asks the model to replace a named span of a given sequence, which is how infilling is done. Scoring averages the log-likelihood of the forward and reverse directions.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper describes 8 sizes from 112M to 46B parameters. Six are released on the Hugging Face hub: progen3-112m, progen3-219m, progen3-339m, progen3-762m, progen3-1b and progen3-3b. The paper states that the weights up to 3B are released and that the ProGen3-46B weights, the dataset and the training code are not. Hugging Face counts the published weights as 112,456,320, 219,677,184, 339,245,568, 762,885,888, 1,355,871,232 and 2,989,920,000 parameters; the paper's table calls the last two 1.4B and 3.0B. None is gated. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision, and for generation also the temperature and top-p, since the README's example sets 0.85 and 0.95 rather than relying on defaults. This page read the 3B checkpoint at revision f2c6b565.

facts.value: For scoring: a FASTA file of sequences, each with a unique id and at most 8190 residues. For generation: a CSV prompt file with an id, a sequence starting with the direction marker 1 or 2, and minimum and maximum new token counts. Infilling prompts add a [GLM] span specification.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Released checkpoints, counted by Hugging Face from the safetensors files: 112,456,320 (progen3-112m), 219,677,184 (219m), 339,245,568 (339m), 762,885,888 (762m), 1,355,871,232 (1b) and 2,989,920,000 (3b). These are total parameters of a sparse model. The paper's Table 3 gives active counts beside each total: 32M of 112M, 63M of 219M, 98M of 339M, 221M of 762M, 393M of 1.4B and 866M of 3.0B, and describes two larger sizes, 10B (2.7B active) and 46B (12.6B active), that are not released.
facts.source_locator: Hugging Face API safetensors totals; paper: Table 3

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Profluent Protein Atlas v1 (PPA-1), which the paper describes as 3.4 billion proteins and 1.1 trillion amino acid tokens drawn from genomic and metagenomic sources, with protein fragments excluded. Sequences are sampled through an Inverse Log scheme over 50% identity clusters. ProGen3-46B was trained on 1.5 trillion tokens from PPA-1; smaller models were trained for fewer tokens, for example ProGen3-339M on 200 billion and ProGen3-3B on 500 billion. The dataset is not released.

run_guide.summary: Install the repository on a GPU machine and score one protein sequence with the 3B checkpoint.
prerequisites: At least one GPU. The developers tested only A100 or H100 cards with at least 40GB of VRAM, and say earlier GPUs may not work because bf16 and flash attention kernels are needed.
The install script builds megablocks 0.7.0 and flash-attn 2.7.4.post1 from source, so a CUDA toolchain is needed. A prepared Docker image is offered instead.
The weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial use only. They are not gated.

steps.title: Score one sequence
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch

from progen3.modeling import ProGen3ForCausalLM
from progen3.batch_preparer import ProGen3BatchPreparer
from progen3.scorer import ProGen3Scorer

model = ProGen3ForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Profluent-Bio/progen3-3b", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
model = model.eval().to("cuda:0")
batch_preparer = ProGen3BatchPreparer()

sequence = "MALWMRLLPLLALLALWGPDPAAAFVNQHLCGSHLVEALYLVCGERGFFYTPKTRREAEDLQVGQVELGGGPGAGSLQPLALEGSLQKRGIVEQCCTSICSLYQLENYCN"

scorer = ProGen3Scorer(model=model)
scores = scorer.score_batch(sequences=[sequence])
print(scores["log_likelihood"][0])
PY
steps.explanation: The README's interactive example, wrapped in a shell heredoc and reduced to the scorer part. It downloads the 3B weights from Hugging Face on first use. The README's logits example is left out.

Building megablocks and flash-attn from source can be slow and needs a matching CUDA toolchain; the Docker image is the alternative the README offers.

notes: The weights licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) differs from the code licence (Apache-2.0), so a commercial user cannot use these weights. The structured context_length 8190 is the scoring limit from the README, not the configuration's max_position_embeddings of 65536 and not the paper's trained context length of 8192 tokens. Revision of 2026-11-27: the full bioRxiv v2 text is now read. It supports the record's description: a sparse family of up to 46B parameters, with the 46B model trained on 1.5T amino acid tokens. The largest released checkpoint is still about 2.99B. The paper's active parameter counts are not put in structured, because no saved file ties an active count to a released checkpoint file.
